links.effect: Combined risk-targeted package increased high-risk retention to 64.0% (RR = 1.45; p < 0.001), +19.9 percentage points from 44.1% baseline.
links.quote: A combined intervention package produced substantially larger gains, increasing retention to 64.0% (RR = 1.45; p < 0.001), corresponding to an absolute improvement of 19.9 percentage points.

links.effect: Two-way texting improved retention to 52.7% (RR = 1.19; p < 0.001); Expert Client support to 55.0% (RR = 1.25; p < 0.001).
links.quote: Individual interventions improved retention to 52.7% with two-way texting (RR = 1.19; p < 0.001) and 55.0% with Expert Client support (RR = 1.25; p < 0.001).

links.effect: Newly initiated: 43.0% to 58.9%; clinically unstable: 28.3% to 39.1%; adolescents: 34.3% to 45.6%, a more modest effect.
links.quote: Intervention effects varied across subgroups, with significant improvements observed among newly initiated patients (43.0% to 58.9%; RR = 1.37; p < 0.001) and clinically unstable patients (28.3% to 39.1%; RR = 1.38; p = 0.01), while effects among adolescents were more modest (34.3% to 45.6%; RR = 1.33; p = 0.03).

screen.practice: risk-based targeting of interventions using predicted risk threshold
screen.reason: The study uses a patient-level Monte Carlo simulation linking an XGBoost predictive risk model to intervention allocation to evaluate the impact and trade-offs of risk-guided targeting strategies for HIV care retention.
